title: Carlsbad structure: the minority attack

D0.outcome: States the app's working definition (pawns on d4 and e3 and no c-pawn for one side, against pawns on c6, d5 and e6; colours may be reversed) and the two standard plans as rules of thumb from the books: the minority attack on the queenside, and play on the kingside or in the centre.

D1.outcome: Told the structure, names each side's standard plan: the b-pawn minority attack for the side with two queenside pawns against three, and the kingside or e-pawn play for the other side (rules of thumb; the app checks only that an evaluation gap exists at a stated depth).

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions with this structure chooses between the minority attack, the e-pawn break and a waiting move, and notices when the minority attack has no target or no time.

D3.outcome: Predicts how one-feature changes (a pair of pieces traded, the c-file already closed, a faster kingside attack) change which plan is right, and checks the verdict with the engine.

misconceptions: The minority attack always produces a weak pawn.
The side facing the minority attack is simply worse.
A backward pawn on a half-open file loses by force.

conditions: Working definition (the app's own, used for recognition practice, not claimed to match any book): one side has pawns on d4 and e3 and no c-pawn, the other has pawns on c6, d5 and e6; the colours may be reversed.

The minority attack (b2-b4-b5 by the side with two queenside pawns against three) aims to exchange on c6 and leave a backward or isolated c-pawn that can be attacked down the half-open c-file; it needs rooks ready for the c-file and time.
The side facing the attack uses the slow plan's time elsewhere: pieces toward the kingside, or an e-pawn break when the d-pawn is loose.
A backward pawn is a tendency, not a verdict: 'invariably lose' is the claim not to teach, and hedgehog-type positions hold backward pawns.
condition_sources: CAP §5 item 17 (flagged; the counter-example is named there from outside knowledge)
contrasts: The minority attack is started while the opponent's kingside play is already faster: the plan is too slow and loses the race.
The exchange on c6 is recaptured so that no pawn is weak: the pawns have been traded for nothing and the plan has produced no target.
The same pieces but the first side still has a c-pawn (for example on c3): this is not the structure and there is no minority attack to run.
